pairs.question: Vultis, ut illos mentitos breviter probem?
pairs.answer: Desperaverunt de languore, cuius remedium, si patri creditis, alius invenit.
pairs.derivation: The speaker poses a real interrogative (vultis... probem?) and immediately supplies the proof as its answer in the next sentence. Answer runs to the first full stop (invenit), which is the complete proof. Nothing cut; the following paragraph (Sive enim...) digresses into the doctor's motives.

pairs.question: Quid hunc sanaverit, vis scire breviter?
pairs.derivation: Within the mother's quoted speech she asks a genuine interrogative (vis scire?) and answers it herself with the closing sententia. Capitalization of Quid normalized; hunc has its referent in the immediately preceding speech (respexit ad vitam, convaluit, evasit). The speech ends here, so nothing follows to cut.

pairs.question: Inventum putatis esse languorem?
pairs.derivation: Real interrogative (putatis?) answered immediately by the next sentence, a pointed correction. Answer is the full sentence to the first stop. What follows (agedum commento tuo, senex...) turns to apostrophizing the father, so the answer window stops here.
